1. The Type D Flip-Flop is designed to store the last input condition until the next input condition is clocked or gated through.
2. A high applied to the D and C inputs sets Q high.
3. A low applied to the D input and a high applied to the C input set Q high.
4. The Type D flip-flop is constructed from NAND or NOR gates that use feedback to produce memory.
NAND GATES
NOR GATESS
5. The active high edge triggered D flip-flop will transfer data to its outputs only when the clock input goes from a low to a high state or a positive going transition (PGT).
6. The active low edge triggered D flip-flop will transfer data to its outputs only when the clock input goes from a high to a low state or a negative going transition (NGT).
